title: pvRibbon
body:
## pvRibbon

Turns lines and polylines (polydata, e.g. streamlines) into flat ribbon strips that follow each line. The ribbon's orientation comes from a normal: the 3-component point array chosen in Vectors, or the fixed DefaultNormal when UseDefaultNormal is true; with neither, VTK computes sliding normals for each line. Width is the half-width; VaryWidth scales it along the line by the Scalars array from Width at the array minimum to twice Width at its maximum, and Angle rotates the ribbon about the line. Use tube or pvTube for round tubes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The Vectors array sets the ribbon normal, not the flow direction; selecting the velocity itself, which is tangent to a streamline, gives degenerate ribbons.
- Lines with duplicate consecutive points, or normals parallel to the line, are skipped; run clean first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Ribbon`. Identity: `filters/RibbonFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Ribbon filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Angle` | The value of this property specifies the offset angle (in degrees) of the ribbon from the line normal. | `{"maximum":360.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `DefaultNormal` | Fixed ribbon normal [nx, ny, nz] applied at every point when UseDefaultNormal is true. It is not used when UseDefaultNormal is false, even if the input has no vector array: VTK then computes sliding normals for each line. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Scalars` | The value of this property indicates the name of the input scalar array used by this filter. The width of the ribbons will be varied based on the values in the specified array if the value of the Width property is 1. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `UseDefaultNormal` | When true, every ribbon is oriented by DefaultNormal regardless of the Vectors array. When false, the selected Vectors array orients the ribbons; if there is none, VTK computes sliding normals along each line. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VaryWidth` | If this property is set to 1, the ribbon width will be scaled according to the scalar array specified in the SelectInputScalars property. Toggle the variation of ribbon width with scalar value. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Vectors` | The value of this property indicates the name of the input vector array used by this filter. If the UseDefaultNormal property is set to 0, the normal vectors for the ribbons come from the specified vector array. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Width` | If the VaryWidth property is set to 1, the value of this property is the minimum ribbon width. If the VaryWidth property is set to 0, the value of this property is half the width of the ribbon. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvRibbon",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
